```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(appusageR)
data(appusage_demo)
```

Use the same sources to compare native formats with standardized tables. Content
selects the parser; filenames provide source identity.

```{r formats}
folder <- system.file("extdata", "synth", package = "appusageR", mustWork = TRUE)
cases <- c("line_seven_days", "meta_seven_days", "day_with_all_totals",
           "app_partial_coverage", "mixed_line_meta")
sources <- appusage_demo$sources[match(cases, appusage_demo$sources$scenario), ]
parsed <- lapply(file.path(folder, sources$source_relpath),
                 run_first_level_appusage, strict = TRUE)
processed <- lapply(parsed, run_second_level_appusage)
counts <- t(vapply(processed, function(x) vapply(x$data, nrow, integer(1)), integer(3)))
rownames(counts) <- cases
counts
expected <- as.matrix(sources[, c("expected_event_rows", "expected_episode_rows",
                                 "expected_daily_rows")])
stopifnot(all(counts == expected))
for (i in seq_along(cases)) {
  stopifnot(identical(processed[[i]]$data, appusage_demo$records[[cases[i]]]$data))
}
```

`line` supplies intervals; `meta` supplies Table 1 summaries and Table 2 events;
`day` and `app` supply daily values. The current second-level defaults reconstruct
pure-meta episodes and retain summary-derived daily totals. Event rows, intervals
and daily aggregates represent the same use at different grains: do not add their
durations together. Day-format `ALL` totals remain as source rows and are excluded
when summing individual apps. App-format totals cover the exported apps.

## Mixed content: default, explicit and legacy selection

```{r mixed}
path <- file.path(folder, sources$source_relpath[5L])
mixed <- parsed[[5L]]
names(mixed$data)
stopifnot(identical(names(mixed$data), c("line", "meta_summary", "meta_events")),
          nrow(mixed$data$meta_events) == 28L,
          sum(processed[[5L]]$data$daily$duration_ms) == 12600000)
head(mixed$data$meta_events)
explicit_line <- run_first_level_appusage(path, type = "line", strict = TRUE)
explicit_meta <- run_first_level_appusage(path, type = "meta", strict = TRUE)
legacy <- run_first_level_appusage(path, type = "legacy", strict = TRUE)
stopifnot(identical(names(explicit_line$data), "line"),
          identical(names(explicit_meta$data), c("meta_summary", "meta_events")),
          identical(legacy$data, explicit_meta$data))
```

Automatic mixed parsing preserves both components: standardized events come from
Table 2, while intervals and daily totals come from line. Explicit `type = "line"`
or `"meta"` selects just that component. Legacy mode applies the historical
single-component choice; it chooses meta in this file. Old saved configurations
with expanded defaults use that compatibility mode. A newly constructed
`appusage_config()` records which meta options were explicitly requested.

```{r explicit-meta-options}
compatible <- run_second_level_appusage(mixed, reconstruct_meta = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(compatible$data, processed[[5L]]$data))
conflict <- tryCatch(run_second_level_appusage(mixed, reconstruct_meta = TRUE),
                     error = identity)
stopifnot(inherits(conflict, "error"))
conditionMessage(conflict)
meta_only <- run_second_level_appusage(explicit_meta, reconstruct_meta = TRUE,
                                      meta_daily_source = "episodes")
stopifnot(nrow(meta_only$data$episode) == 14L)
```

Explicit reconstruction of a mixed source conflicts with its native line
intervals. Select meta first when reconstruction is the intended analysis.
`?appusage_configuration` documents the argument-origin rules and the
`summary`, `episodes`, and `both` daily choices.

## Units, row order and tail configuration

The faithful Table 2 retains event order and the source configuration tail.
Inspect these fields before interpreting event-to-episode reconstruction.

```{r event-contract}
events <- mixed$data$meta_events
names(events)
standard_events <- processed[[5L]]$data$event
stopifnot(all(standard_events$event_type == rep(c(1, 2, 1, 2), 7L)),
          all(diff(standard_events$source_line) > 0),
          all(standard_events$configuration_tail == "orientation=portrait,demo=synthetic"))
head(standard_events[, c("source_line", "event_type", "configuration_tail")])
raw_lines <- readLines(path, encoding = "UTF-8", warn = FALSE)
tail(raw_lines, 6L)
stopifnot(any(grepl("orientation=portrait", raw_lines, fixed = TRUE)),
          any(grepl("demo=synthetic", raw_lines, fixed = TRUE)))
line <- processed[[1L]]$data
stopifnot(inherits(line$daily$date, "Date"), is.numeric(line$daily$duration_ms),
          nrow(line$event) == 0L, nrow(line$episode) == 14L)
line$daily[, c("date", "package_name", "duration_ms")]
```

Numeric `*_ms` columns retain milliseconds. Datetimes retain their timezone;
calendar dates are `Date`. A typed empty event table in a line export means the
format supplies no event grain. It does not mean the person had zero events.
